title: Over the Pass
story:
Dawn came in a hush of damp spruce needles. James stepped out of the stone trailhead shelter, tightening the strap of his map canister across his chest and testing the cool mountain air. Behind him, Pinecrest Stream rushed over smooth river pebbles, its churning song already fading as the rocky switchbacks pulled him upward into the thinning mist.

The trail climbed steeply, winding through towering highland pines draped in silver moss and wild bromeliads. He felt the damp, cool grit beneath his paws. He felt the crisp alpine breeze bite gently at his nose. He felt the steady swing of the brass canister ticking softly against his flank like a small, familiar companion. With each turn of the switchback, the canopy broke apart, offering glimpses of the sprawling valley below until Oakhaven’s bridges, roofs, and even the domed crown of the Grand Library shrank into distant, geometric toys.

By early afternoon, the trees gave way to wind-battered tussock grass, slate boulders, and a sudden rush of cold sky. James reached the narrow saddle where the old mountain road crossed the mountain spine: Cloudveil Pass. Pulling out his brass compass, he held it steady in both paws. The slender needle trembled, pointing faithfully back toward the town and the friends he had left behind, while the worn dirt path tumbled downward ahead of him, snaking toward unfamiliar southern valleys and terraced hillsides.

James stood upon a flat stone at the crest, looking out across the vast sweep of green ridges fading into purple haze. Standing tall against the mountain wind, he murmured his quiet, familiar greeting: "Pleased to meet you, whatever comes next." High overhead, a solitary highland hawk caught a thermal, banking south toward horizons he had never seen.
